request.spec:
Two snapshot dates can be compared: a from-date, a to-date and a button list, per person in list
order, <name> <then> <now>: `then` is the due-total of the SNAPSHOT written when the sheet's today
was changed away from the from-date (empty when there is none), `now` is likewise the snapshot for
the to-date, or the person's due-total now when the to-date is blank.

agent.result_text:
I added the snapshot comparison, but `bin/e2e` does not pass: 1 of the 4 tests passes and 3 fail. Each failure is an assertion in the spec that no app can satisfy. I didn't change the spec to get around them.

**The change.** It's one new front-end file, `src/main/frontend/features/snapshots/compare.slot.tsx`. The app already saved a snapshot of each person's due-total whenever the sheet's today changed, so no database, server or audit changes were needed.
- It adds a from-date (`snapshot-from`), a to-date (`snapshot-to`) and a button (`snapshot-compare`) to the sheet.
- Pressing the button re-reads the stored snapshots and shows one `snapshot-line` per person, in list order, as `<name> <then> <now>`.
- `then` is that person's snapshot for the from-date, or empty if there isn't one.
- `now` is their snapshot for the to-date. If the to-date is blank, it's their current due-total, worked out the same way as the people CSV export does it.
- If today was changed away from the same date more than once, the latest snapshot for that date is used.

**Why the 3 tests fail:**
1. **"snapshot comparison", line 24.** It expects `"Ada  "` with two trailing spaces. The test helper trims each line's text before comparing, so the app's `"Ada  "` comes back as `"Ada"` and can never match. I made a temporary copy of this test with only that one value changed to `["Ada", "Ben"]`. It passed in full: every comparison, including the one after moving to 2026-03-11, and the whole audit check. I deleted the copy afterwards.
2. **"scenario 1" (line 183) and "scenario 3" (line 1401).** They expect `sheet-parent` to show the literal text `"__SHEET__-p"`. That's a placeholder that was never filled in; the app correctly shows the real sheet id, e.g. `smvl6603jhhuy-p`. Neither scenario reaches the snapshot comparison at all.

"Scenario 2" passes unchanged.

**Port clash.** My first run failed at the very first actions because another app on this machine was using port 3000, so the tests were talking to the wrong server. Later runs used `PORT=3017 bin/e2e`.

To get the suite green, the spec needs line 24 fixed and `__SHEET__` replaced at lines 183, 332 and 1401. I'm not allowed to edit it, so that's for whoever maintains the test.
